evidence: impact-chain-gate.rb's table_data_anchor_valid checks whether the anchor survives in that same path at base, then validates its current explicit table data-cell location. The documented control proves a new locator at the changed firing path and location/shape, not owner-wide semantic novelty or truth of an author's RED declaration.

An actual earlier-candidate helper control, substituting only in-memory blob providers, returned true for a new definition, false for a same-file surviving anchor and true for text present in another owner file. This mechanical observation remains preserved; it is not recast as a rejection the gate performs.

The older normative-list locator also did not promise owner-wide novelty. Moving existing guidance into an actual firing surface can change behavior. Requiring an owner-wide semantic or text duplication classifier would add a new contract rather than repair the documented same-path predicate. Current self-register and HTML fixes retain this boundary.
